packages.vo: Link Click just dropped its final trailer before Season 3 returns today, and it confirms this mystery traces back to Cheng Xiaoshi's own father. Season 3 Part One drops August 14 on Crunchyroll as the front half of a full twenty-four episode story, doubling the length of every prior season combined, with Part Two expected in 2027. Season 2 ended with Cheng Xiaoshi and Lu Guang chasing the Bahati fire case, which the show's own synopsis ties directly to Xiaoshi's father Cheng Weimin and mother Shao Yuanyuan, while Xia Fei's disappearance stayed unresolved. Part One picks that exact thread up immediately. A new Bridon officer named Jae joins the investigation, and Season 3 also brings back Vein as Qiao Ling's photograph-based powers keep on awakening, per the show's own synopsis. This is also the donghua sitting at an eight point seven seven average on MyAnimeList, praised for doing something Chinese animation rarely gets credit for internationally, and it's already been nominated for multiple international animation awards, including the Crunchyroll Anime Awards and the Tokyo Anime Awards Festival. So does doubling the episode count change how deep this mystery goes, or does it just double how long you're stuck waiting to find out? Leave your take.

Season 3 is a 24-episode split-cour with Part One covering the first 12 episodes and Part Two expected in 2027.
Season 2 ended with the Bahati fire case, which the show's own synopsis ties directly to Cheng Xiaoshi's father Cheng Weimin and mother Shao Yuanyuan, while Xia Fei's disappearance stayed unresolved.

A new Bridon officer named Jae joins the investigation, and Season 3 brings back Vein as Qiao Ling's photograph-based powers keep awakening -- per the show's own Season 3 synopsis, not a trailer-specific visual claim.
Link Click holds an 8.77 average on MyAnimeList and has been nominated for multiple international animation awards, including the Crunchyroll Anime Awards and the Tokyo Anime Awards Festival.
